This form must be executed in duplicate when a child is transferred from a reservation to a nonreservation school. The Superintendent of the nonreservation school will retain the original for his files, and the duplicate shall be deposited in the reservation school records. The reservation superintendent should send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate as provided by law. All the blanks must be properly filled in every case. If the information called for on any part of the blank is not known, that fact should be stated. No space should be left unfilled. Whether the patient is living or dead, their names must be given. The person who signs the blank as consenting to the transfer should indicate his relation to the applicant by marking out the word "parent," "guardian," or "next of kin," leaving unmarked only the title appropriate to the signer. INDORSEMENTS. The laws relating to the transfer of Indian children from reservations and schools are as follows: That hereafter no Indian child shall be sent from any Indian reservation to a school beyond the State or Territory in which said reservation is situated without the voluntary consent of the father or mother of such child if either of them are living, and if neither of them are living without the voluntary consent of the next of kin of such child. Such consent shall be made before the agent of the reservation, and he shall send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate that such consent has been voluntarily given before such child shall be removed from such reservation. And it shall be unlawful for any Indian agent or other employee of the Government to induce, or seek to induce, by withholding rations or by other improper means, the parents or next of kin of any Indian to consent to the removal of any Indian child beyond the limits of any reservation. (28 Stats., p. 906.) Provided, That hereafter no Indian child shall be taken from any school in any State or Territory to a school in any other State against its will or without the written consent of its parents. (29 Stats., p. 348.) That no Indian pupil under the age of fourteen years shall be transported at Government expense to any Indian school beyond the limits of the State or Territory in which the parents of such child reside or of the adjoining State or Territory. (35 Stat. L., 781.) The rules provide that— A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. An Indian boy or girl 18 years old and over may, without the consent of parents or others, personally sign the application form on its being changed to suit the case; but in all cases where the parents are living they should first be consulted. This form is to be used only in transfers from reservations or Indian schools to nonreservation schools. RECORD OF PUPIL IN SCHOOL RECORD OF Juanita V. Boyd (Name) at Cushman Trades School. Keith Falls, Wash. Route 1 Box 449 Mr. C.H. Hammond July 1st '1918 Dear Sir, I instructed the Bank to send $56.00 to your credit for two full fare and three half fare tickets for my five children. Tickets would amount to about $46.00 or $13.28 for full fare and about $6.70 for half fare. Balance for expenses if you should get this before you send the children they could day till after the 4th of July if they wished and you could give them $3.00 for the 4th. Please telegraph me. when they will arrive at Myers Falls. And if possible have them arrive in daylight as it is a 14 mi drive and cannot ferry the Columbia at night. Thanking you for favor received I beg to remain, Truly, Mrs Maggie Boyd. Kettle Falls Wm Route 1. Box 49 Aug. 29th 1917 Mr. Wilson, Dear Sir: In reply to your letter will say I have five children the same who I made applications previously. I do not know of any other Indian children who wish to attend school now but will inquire and if I find any will make a report to you of same. My nearest railroad station is Moyers Falls. I would like to send the children about Sept 10. I hope you will be able to send the transportation subject to a few days delay if necessary as I may not be able to make instant preparation also will the children compelled to travel alone or will someone travel with them. Thanking you for past favor and patience as to my many inquiries I beg to remain Truly Mrs Maggie Boyd Sept. 6, 1917. Mrs. Maggie Boyd, Route 1, Box 49, Kettle Falls, Wn. Dear Madam: I have placed an order for five tickets, two full fares and three half fares at Myers Falls, subject to your order for the transportation of your children to Cushman School. I do not know of any representative in your immediate vicinity who could accompany your children. I suggest that you write to Mr. Victor H. Johnson, Daisy, Washington, asking him when the party of pupils from his locality intend to start for Cushman. It is possible that you can arrange to have your children take the same train. Pupils from his locality may take the train at Addy. If this arrangement cannot be made, I suggest you arrange to accompany your children to Spokane and see that they get on the proper train for Tacoma. If you will advise me by wire, when these children start, I will meet them at the depot in Tacoma. Very respectfully, Superintendent. OHK(KM) Kettle Falls, Wash. Route 1, Box 49 Aug 1st, '17. Mr. Wilson, Dear Sir - As it is now drawing near time for school to commence I deem it wise to write you in regards to my children's transportation etc. I wish to send them the first part of September. Truly, Mrs. Maggie Boyd. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE CUSHMAN INDIAN TRADES SCHOOL, Tacoma, Wash. Aug. 8, 1917 Mrs. Maggie Boyd, Kettle Falls, Wash Dear Madam:- I have your letter of the 1st instant inquiring about transportation for your children. I have to report that the Commissioner has not yet sent me any money to pay transportation, but I am expecting it soon. Let me know how many children you wish to send and the railroad station from which they will start, and I will arrange for their transportation as soon as funds are received. Are there any more Indian children in that community that want to attend this school, if so I will arrange for them to come at the same time your children do. Very respectfully, Superintendent. Kettle Falls, Wm. Route 1 Box 49 March 16-1917 Superintendent Ind. School. Dear Sir, Yours of March 13th at hand and in reply: My nearest railroad station is Meyers Falls, Wash. I sent the applications for four of my children and some days later sent application for another the fifth and last. In case she is also called will she travel alone or will there be others. Truly, Mrs. Fannie Smith Boyd. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington. March 13, 1917. Mrs. Fannie Smith Boyd, Kettle Falls, Washington. Dear Madam: I am in receipt of your applications for the enrollment of four children in this school and the applications have been accepted by the Physician, but I am waiting for instructions from the Department before placing transportation for your children. As soon as I get their instructions I will place transportation and in the mean time I would like to know your nearest railroad point so that I will know where to send the tickets. Very respectfully, Superintendent. TBW/C Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington. April 10, 1917. Mrs. Fannie Smith Boyd, Kettle Falls, Washington. Dear Madam: I received your application for the enrollment of your children in this school and would be very glad to accept all of them if it were not for the fact that I am compelled to close the school on the 15th of this month. I would have answered your letter sooner, but the question of continuing the school was not settled until today. I am indeed sorry that I cannot take your children this year, but would be glad to have them any time after the first of July. The date of opening of the next term is September 10, 1917, and I would be glad if they could be here on that date. Very respectfully, Superintendent. 5-297 c LAUNDERING. RECORD CARD—PREVOCATIONAL DIVISION. Each girl should devote 15 weeks to the work of this department during the three prevocational years. When she has accomplished the work as outlined in the course of study in a satisfactory manner, a suitable rating should be recorded. Ratings must be based on a practical application as well as a knowledge of the principles involved. Ratings should be excellent (E), good (G), fair (F). If pupil's work is not worthy of a rating of fair, no grade should be recorded. Under "Remarks" mention anything that indicates interest, conduct, and proficiency of the pupil. This card should be filed in folder for record of pupil (5-197). When the pupil is transferred to another school a copy of this card should be sent to the officer in charge of the school to which she is transferred.
